description: Event system, enhanced tool registry schema, pending-key model, and extended adapter contract. This establishes the core data structures and models that all subsequent features build upon.
steps: Create recontool/engine/__init__.py as the new event-driven engine package

Create recontool/engine/events.py with typed event classes: ScanRequested, ToolSelected, ToolDependencyChecked, ToolReady, ToolBlocked, ToolRunning, ToolArtifactProduced, EntityDiscovered, PendingKeyCreated, PendingKeyResolved, ToolCompleted, ToolFailed, ScanCompleted. Use dataclasses with timestamp, scan_id, correlation_id fields. Include an EventBus class (in-process pub/sub with async handlers).

Create recontool/engine/registry.py with an enhanced ToolSpec model (Pydantic BaseModel) capturing all required fields from the spec: name, category, purpose, version, install_method, runtime_dependencies, invocation_strategy, supported_input_types, required_inputs, optional_inputs, output_types, output_file_paths, stdout_semantics, json_schema, concurrency_safety, idempotency, timeout, retry_policy (max_retries, backoff_factor, retryable_errors), rate_limit_constraints, parallel_safe, incremental_safe, produces_entities, unlocks_pending_keys, triggers_downstream, validation_status, test_coverage_status, documentation_status. Include a ToolRegistry class that loads from config/tools.yaml + config/tools_generic.yaml and provides lookup by name, category, phase, input_type, output_type.

Create recontool/engine/pending_keys.py with the pending-key model. PendingKey dataclass: key_type (e.g. 'subdomain', 'live_host', 'url'), key_value, created_by_tool, created_at, resolved_at, resolved_by_tool, scan_id, status (pending/resolved/expired). PendingKeyStore class that persists to DB (new table) and provides: create_key(), resolve_key(), get_pending_for_tool(), get_resolved_keys(), is_tool_ready(). Rules: if required keys missing -> tool pending; new keys produced -> dependents reschedulable; all keys available -> schedule tool.

Create recontool/engine/models.py with SQLAlchemy models: ToolRun (id, scan_id, tool_name, status, started_at, finished_at, input_fingerprint, output_fingerprint, exit_code, artifact_paths JSON, entity_count, retry_count, error_detail, duration_ms, command_executed), PendingKeyRecord (id, scan_id, key_type, key_value, status, created_by_tool, resolved_by_tool, created_at, resolved_at, fingerprint), ScanState (id, scan_id, status, iteration, depth, started_at, updated_at, checkpoint_json JSON).

Extend recontool/adapters/base.py Adapter class with new optional methods that default to no-ops for backwards compatibility: install_check(self) -> bool, prepare(self, ctx) -> None, validate_inputs(self, inputs) -> list[str] (returns validation errors), build_command(self, ctx) -> str|None, parse_stdout(self, stdout: str) -> dict, parse_files(self, paths: list[str]) -> dict, emit_normalized_events(self, parsed: dict) -> list[Event], map_outputs_to_entities(self, parsed: dict) -> list[Event], resolve_pending_keys(self, parsed: dict) -> list[str], can_run_in_parallel(self) -> bool, dependencies(self) -> list[str], timeout_seconds(self) -> int, retry_policy(self) -> dict. These are optional overrides - existing adapters continue to work via their run() method.
Add DB migration support: update recontool/core/db.py create_all() to include the new engine models table creation alongside existing models.
acceptance_criteria: EventBus can register handlers and dispatch events asynchronously
ToolSpec validates a complete tool entry from config/tools.yaml
ToolRegistry loads all tools from both YAML files
PendingKeyStore can create, query, and resolve pending keys
New SQLAlchemy models (ToolRun, PendingKeyRecord, ScanState) create tables successfully
Existing Adapter subclasses continue to work without modification (backwards compat)
